chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Flax (linen) was for the Children of Israel, they were enshrouded with it, and cotton is for the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.الْقُطْنُ: Cotton, the plant fiber used for fabric and shrouds
key_terms.الْكَتَّانُ: Flax or linen, a plant fiber used for fabric and shrouds
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُونَ بِهِ: They are enshrouded with it (passive verb referring to burial shrouds)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended material for Muslim shrouds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the concept of *khasasiyya* (specificity) in Islamic jurisprudence, assigning cotton as the preferred shroud material for the Muslim Ummah while acknowledging linen's historical use by the Children of Israel. Scholars often interpret this not merely as a material preference but as a sign of the distinct identity and divine favor granted to the Prophet's community, reinforcing the Sunnah of using locally available, pure materials for burial rites.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The flax (linen) was for the Children of Israel, they were enshrouding with it, and the cotton is for the community of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Hashim from abu Khadijah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The Israelites used silk for shroud; and cotton is for the followers of the Holy prophet, Muhammad, O Allah grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
